title: The Strand away from the strip

p: Brookgreen Gardens, just south of Murrells Inlet, was founded in 1931 by Archer and Anna Hyatt Huntington on four former rice plantations. It is a sculpture garden and wildlife preserve with more than 1,400 works of American figurative sculpture, and the garden paths are laid out in the shape of a butterfly. It is big enough that you will want to plan more than an hour. Pick a few sections and slow down.

Hobcaw Barony, near Georgetown, is a 16,000-acre preserve that was once Bernard Baruch's winter retreat. You can only visit by guided tour, and the main tours require reservations, so plan ahead. Vereen Memorial Gardens in Little River and Waites Island are quieter places to stretch your legs.

Myrtle Beach State Park and Huntington Beach State Park are the two big public parks on the Strand. Both have beach access, trails and wildlife. Huntington Beach is known for birding and for alligators in its freshwater lagoons, and it also holds Atalaya Castle.

Dolphins live along this coast year-round. Visit Myrtle Beach says sightings are more common during the fall migration, and sources disagree about the best month, so treat any promise of guaranteed sightings carefully. Dolphin cruises leave from Murrells Inlet and Little River, with trips that run from about an hour to two hours. Kayak and paddleboard outfitters like Surf the Earth, Great Escapes and Black River Outdoors offer calmer ways to explore the marsh and the blackwater rivers.
The MarshWalk in Murrells Inlet is a half-mile boardwalk over the salt marsh. It is free to walk, and it is the best place on the Strand to watch a sunset over the marsh.
Alligator Adventure, T.I.G.E.R.S. and Wild Woods Farm are the animal attractions. They are different in scale and style, so read each listing before you pick one. Wild Woods Farm runs by appointment.

list: Bring bug spray, especially in warm months and near the marsh.
Tides change what you can do in the marsh. Ask kayak outfitters about tide timing.
Check each park or preserve's page for hours, fees and any trail closures. Huntington Beach's marsh boardwalk, for instance, has been closed for construction in the past.
